text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Charge 2 Heart Rate + Fitness Wristband, Teal, Small (US Version) My husband purchased this for me for Christmas. I like the tracker, it is a better-looking device than the old Charge HR and does a decent job tracking steps, HR, etc. but has some flaws. HR is relatively accurate, but at times, and only when I am walking versus doing high-intensity workouts, the device will say that my HR is over 180 when my max HR for high-intensity cardio is more like 168. It also tends to under-count my steps, which I think is preferable to over-counting them, but still annoying. Also, it is hard to get my Charge 2 to switch between screens by "tapping it". It normally takes having to tap it really hard to get it to switch screens. Other than that, it gives me a rough estimate for my steps for the day, encourages me to move frequently (with the 250 steps/hr function), and gives me an idea of my HR during various exercises (not super accurate, but I'm only looking for a ballpark estimate/compare my HR across activities).

That said, the biggest physical flaw I'm seeing is with the new band attachment method. When I got my tracker new, I noticed that on one side of the tracker, the band wasn't attaching as tightly as the other. I didn't think much of it at the time, but over the course of five months, it has gotten progressively worse to the point that one side of the band will easily be "bumped" off the tracker and the whole device will detach from my wrist. I notified customer service about the issue and they did send me a new band free of charge, however, it was like pulling teeth to get them to replace a $30 band. I first received an e-mail from CS stating that I needed to take a photo of the problem with my case number present in the photo as well as the FitBit logo on my device, which was no small feat to accomplish given the location of my band's issue. I did take the photo for them (though it took two sets of hands to get everything in the photo the way CS wanted it), but I felt that the process of getting a replacement band was very frustrating and put a lot of ridiculous demands on the consumer to "prove" the problem, only to simply replace a $30 band.

In any case, I recommend the FitBit - it's not a perfect device, and customer service from the company is overly frustrating to fix a problem that's well-known (check the FitBit boards) and cheap for the company to fix without making the customer jump through flaming hoops.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Charge 2 Heart Rate + Fitness Wristband, Teal, Small (US Version)

Proform Power 1080 Treadmill Proform Power 1080 Treadmill is a large treadmill with enough extra features to make workouts more enjoyable and more likely to take place. This treadmill is much more than a simple belt with readout of time and distance. Proform made this treadmill more sophisticated with multiple options, different workout plans, and added accessories to keep your workout running smoothly.

The Proform Power 1080 Treadmill is a high- tech machine and it has several different walking/jogging routines to suit your exercise needs. You can select what you want, tailored to your own needs, and perform your workout. The Proform Power 1080 Treadmill includes four main workout option categories: calorie burning workout, all- terrain, set a goal, and iFit, which uses wifi. No matter which option you use, the treadmill provides you with a full report showing your distance, average speed, elapsed time, vertical feet climbed, heart rate, and more.

Those who have not worked out much should probably begin with the set a goal workout or the calorie burning workout. The set a goal option lets you define a goal based on distance, time, or calorie- burning. The calorie- burning workout goes straight for the gut, letting you select a number of calories you would like to burn using pre- set options which can be adjusted to your own desired levels. These two are self- defined options make things easy through the use of defaulted settings, but you can still change them to suit your desires. For example, I may select a workout goal of 1 mile. The treadmill will default to a basic workout with inclines, varying speeds, etc. If I like, I can make a slight adjustment and, for example, change the time from 18 minutes to 12 and remove any percentage inclines. This is nice because the added flexibility lets you create a workout that is just right for you. Even after a workout has started, you can still make adjustments to the speed and percentage incline by pushing a button.

For the more advanced and/or more adventurous, this Proform treadmill has you covered. The iFit Live accesses more challenging workouts that are completely varied and the treadmill will change speed and incline on its own with greater frequency than you get with the calorie burning workout or other options. The idea is to make the experience similar to what you would go through if you were jogging through a place with varied hills, speeds, etc. It even accesses Google Maps to create a workout based on a specific location. The iFit feature requires accessing your wifi so it does take a little preparation, but the live action makes this one of the more enjoyable features of this treadmill. Once you setup an account, it remembers you and what you did the last time. It even keeps track of different family members and then reminds each of what they did before and what phase of the workout is next phase so that each person can pick up where they left off.

The Proform Power 1080 Treadmill is certainly a very cool, very modern treadmill, but is there anything that Proform overlooked or that needs improvement? Well, yes, there are a few things. One problem is the fan. The treadmill has a built- in fan and while this is certainly a good idea, the fan is far too weak to make it useful and there is no way to aim the air directly at your face. You need a second and better source of air than this to keep you cooled down and focused. Another surprising oversight is the lack of a holder for a water bottle. There are two square- shaped places where a beverage may be placed, but the shape isn't round and thus it will not hold a round bottle very securely. A third possible problem area for some is the time it takes for the screen to boot up. I find that the touch screen is responsive and works well, but it takes up to a minute after the power is turned on before the screen responds.

Exercising is certainly important and the Proform Power 1080 Treadmill is a very good, very sturdy treadmill with many features that work to encourage exercise. It isn't perfect, but with many cool and useful features like iFit, customized controls, sound systems for your iPod or MP3 player, and a solid warranty, this treadmill has much going for it and makes a very good choice for your next piece of exercise equipment.
text_fidelity_b: Proform Power 1080 Treadmill

text_fidelity_a:
Slime 10056W Bike Tube Puncture Repair Sealant, Prevent and Repair, Suitable for All Bicycles, Non-Toxic, Eco-Friendly, 16oz Bottle Used it, Loved it ... on the single wheel on my electric unicycle (EUC).
Where the rubber meets the road, it seems, doesn't get enough love here. So I thought I'd start a thread to share opinions about tire pressure, maintenance, etc. (starting with some of my opinions).

I find tire pressure to be one of the most important components of handling and ride, and I'm a bit obsessive about it on my EUC's (probably carrying over from motorcycles and bikes). There are three things that make tire pressure a challenge with EUC's:

EUC's only have one tire, low pressure has a direct impact on ride, and tire failures are unforgiving
EUC's have unique bent valve stems that make it hard to find inner-tubes, and a pain to fill (you just don't want to do it)
EUC tire pressure is a bother to check compared to any other vehicle, because the valve stems are hidden in the EUC cavity, and difficult to attach to a pump
... and there are probably other things. The net result is that you want to maintain the tire, fill to pressure and forget it.

To that end, I've Slimed (https://www.amazon.com/Slime-10056-Tube-Sealant-oz/dp/B003V9XYNW/ref=sr_1_2?ie=UTF8&qid=1487706156&sr=8-2&keywords=slime+bicycle) both my V8 and Zero. I used about 1/3rd of the bottle on each one. There is no effect whatsoever on the feel of the wheel, and I think it provides a certain security. In Chicago, I can take my bike into any number of convenient shops to buy and install a new inner-tube; but the same shops would just draw a blank with an EUC, and the inner-tubes are hard to find. Best to maintain what you have.

I like to keep my tire pressure up at 3 bar (~44 psi). The sidewalls of my V8 and Zero tires both recommend 40-65psi pressure, and the V8 comes from the factory at 2.8 bar (~40psi). So for me 3 bar seems the right pressure, and both wheels feel good at that pressure. It's a real bother to fit a pressure gauge on the valve stem because they are bent against the wheel. I almost never get a seal on my gauge without several tries.

So instead, I pumped the wheels up with my Lezyne pump (https://www.amazon.com/Lezyne-Steel-Floor-Drive-Black/dp/B005UND3CY/ref=sr_1_3?ie=UTF8&qid=1487706504&sr=8-3&keywords=lezyne+pump) -- I recommend Lesyzne as the absolute best bike pump on the market -- and then put a Gozens 44psi cap (https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B01HRIKIY0/ref=oh_aui_detailpage_o04_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1) on the wheel. That way, I can easily check the pressure at the start of each ride. You do need to buy the Gozens at a particular pressure (BTW, they have bluetooth systems, which I think are a bit of overkill) but you get 4 of the basic caps for $9, so NBD.
text_fidelity_b: Slime 10056W Bike Tube Puncture Repair Sealant, Prevent and Repair, Suitable for All Bicycles, Non-Toxic, Eco-Friendly, 16oz Bottle

text_fidelity_a:
Prevention Best of Yoga DVD: Yoga Training At Home. - Perfect Yoga Program For Toning, Breathing, Meditating, Relaxing, Balancing, Improving Your Core Strength, and More! If you want to feel more alive in your body with deep breathing and strengthening plus stretching you may enjoy the postures and dynamic movements in these yoga and Pilates inspired workouts. You may want to do one or more routines as time allows. I started with three workouts from level one. I did 2, 5 and 3 in that order and it was perfect. Level one seems for people who are familiar with yoga but want a slower pace and less strenuous exercises and postures.

2 - 15 minutes - Chair Yoga is perfect for beginners who want to do the poses with the support of a chair. The stretches are for the upper and lower body. This felt so good.

5 - 11 minutes - Movement Medicine stretches out the neck, shoulders and back. You will need a mat and strap to do this effectively. I especially loved the calming music.

3 - 20 minutes - Yoga for Calm has serene relaxing music. Instead of a bolster I put two yoga blocks side by side with a blanket on top. That worked. When using blankets under my back I also needed a block to put my head on. On my back, I used two folded blankets in place of the bolster and a rolled up towel under my neck with two blocks under my knees. The restorative poses go by fast!

You may want to do these next four all in one day too, I did it and it was great!

1 - 24 minutes - Yoga for Strength has all the classic poses like mountain pose, downward facing dog, warrior and cobra. When the instructor went flat on her stomach I did cat/cow instead. This workout seemed very intermediate to be honest. There were no real modifications for beginners besides it was slower and you could use yoga blocks when needed.

4 - 8 minutes - Core Blast - You will feel this all in your core and it is a short routine so you can put all your effort into just a few minutes. You do need to be on your knees for part of it but if you use a blanket that helps. Plus you need to be on your back and do an extended plank pose. I took breaks!

6 - 5 minutes - Quick Fix for Back pain is not a relaxing workout to stretch out your back, it is more preventative so you strengthen your back. It uses a chair!

7 - 6 minutes - Guided Meditation is a relaxing way to end your workouts. This is quieting and good if you are stressed out and just want to breathe deeply. There was no prayer or chanting so I'd say it was non religious meditation which I prefer.

Level 2 is a whole other story! These routines are best if you are intermediate and know your way around a yoga posture.

Total Body Yoga - 9 minutes - Selena Watkins is a very knowledgeable and fit instructor who has you standing tall and then rolling down to touch the floor. There is some ballet inspired work and it is generally flowing from one pose to another. You will recognize child's pose and reverse plank.

Hips and Abs - 10 minutes - This has Pilates inspired moves or maybe some Pilates is inspired by yoga! You will recognize plank, side plank, child's pose, downward facing dog and half pigeon. You need a lot of ab strength to do this workout.

Bends and Twists - 10 minutes - You need to be able to lay flat on your belly and do up dog which to me is more advanced. Bow appears and then you are flat on your back. Maybe in my 20s I could do some of the upside down yoga poses. Not anymore after 50!

Strengthen and Stretch - 22 minutes - Downward dog turns into a balance challenge and there are lots of forward bends. Plank and cat/cow are familiar.

Stretch and Tone - 11 minutes - Forward bends and intense stretches are what you have to look forward to. You will be moving from cobra to child's pose.

Then arrives Level 3 - This is for serious students of yoga who want to push themselves just that little bit further and do longer workouts that require balance, endurance and arm strength!

1 - 30 minutes - Let It Go Yoga - This was almost more intermediate for the most part however. Plank pose, downward dog, up dog and low lunges are easier. It is the bridge pose that is difficult. Over 50 you may need a towel for your knees. There is lots of stretching and some balance postures.

2 - 11 minutes - Anytime Yoga is cute with a home setting and an orange couch which has visual appeal. You will be doing plank, downward facing dog, upward facing dog and down dog split which is more challenging. You flow from one pose to another and it requires strength and flexibility.

3 - 30 minutes - Power Flow is probably the most complex and toughest workout to do on all the DVDs. There are things I'd never seen done in a yoga workout before. The sun salutations require good arm strength and there are numerous forward bends if you enjoy that the best! The calming music is good because this workout is an endurance test. It is a very original sequence of moves designed for the most fit individual who wants a challenge. Definitely advanced!

All of the instructors in these DVD workouts are super fit and trim. Amy Ippoliti had the most calming routines for Level 1. It was nice to see Christ Fraytag doing stretching. Rebecca Pacheco does everything perfectly and precisely - she is a joy to workout with. Selena Watkins is super strong and flexible. Tara Stiles does yoga in a high-rise with incredible views.

Things you will want to have on hand when doing all these workouts include: a soft blanket, a chair, a sticky mat, yoga blocks, a yoga strap and an optional bolster. I do not have a bolster so substituted blocks and a blanket.

So whether you are level 1, 2 or 3 there is something to enjoy. The workouts are short enough that you can do one or two or even more in a row. I do wish they'd put a meditation session on each DVD and not just the first so if you want a meditation session after a workout you don't have to put DVD 1 back in. But it is a minor thing. There is also no extended corpse poses to relax at the end of each workout. But you can just do it yourself as the workouts end.

~The Rebecca Review
text_fidelity_b: Prevention Best of Yoga DVD: Yoga Training At Home. - Perfect Yoga Program For Toning, Breathing, Meditating, Relaxing, Balancing, Improving Your Core Strength, and More!

text_fidelity_a:
HemingWeigh Highly Absorbant Microfiber Yoga and Exercise Hand Towel I'm very pleased with both the hand towel and the yoga mat towel. Both share the same type of fabric -- smooth, but with far more texture than the typical microfiber. That is a major plus on three fronts: it allows it to absorb water faster; it holds more water; and, in the case of the mat towel, provides for grip against slipping on the mat.

The construction quality for both is excellent. The fabric is thick and there's a well-stitched hem that is folded over so that it doesn't feel scratchy or catch on anything.

The hand towel is nicely sized (roughly 15 inches wide and 24 inches long) making it big enough to be very effective for face and hand drying. Smaller towels make you feel like you're dabbing away with a tissue - this feels more like a real towel. The mat towel is about 72 inches by 24 inches, which is more than ample enough to cover my mat.

Microfiber is great stuff for the gym since it absorbs quickly and drys fast. It's also very compact - I can roll up the hand towel ans stow it in my bag without taking up hardly any room. The mat towel is a bit more bulky, but it's still very easy to tote along with my mat. Much, much easier than a regular terry towel, and it provides much better protection against slipping on the mat than a terry towel.

In addition to gym use, it can also be used for a lot of other tasks. I like to keep the hand towel handy when I'm doing yard work in the summer - great for mopping up the sweat. It's also fantastic for keeping cool (wet it with the hose, wring it out, and drape it your head and neck. Yes, you'll look stupid, but you'll also be cool and comfortable). The mat towel is also good to have in the car to drape over the seats when you're carrying something messy (or potentially messy, such as a dog). Very absorbent should spills occur; easy to wash; and takes up very little room when folded.

These are very versatile and nicely made towels. I would highly recommend both.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: HemingWeigh Highly Absorbant Microfiber Yoga and Exercise Hand Towel

Valeo Padded Ocelot Lifting Gloves, Gym Gloves, Workout Gloves, Exercise Gloves for Powerlifting, Cross Training, Rowing for Men & Women I've been using these for a few weeks and am happy with them. I measured my hand to be 8.5-8.75" and ordered XLarge based on the sizing chart. They are a good fit. Not great, but good. If anything, they might be a tad large, but that's mostly solved with the adjustable velcro strap.

The only serious drawback I've noticed is that when I bench-press, the left glove pinches my skin between my thumb and index finger. It's not so bad that I can't lift or I'd want to go back to lifting without the gloves. And, I don't get the pinching with other lifts. But, it's annoying and part of the reason I'm giving 4 stars.

Otherwise, I really like these gloves. I use them with free weights and feel that my grip is better and I can focus more on the strength exercise. Without gloves, I had to concentrate more on gripping the weight. And, my hands would hurt somewhat after lifting without the gloves. As others have noted, the padding is great for gripping unpadded rods and bar. All the weights I use are unpadded (just a textured metal rod) and I find the glove padding helpful. I wouldn't want to use these with a padded rod or bar as I think that they would not improve grip in that case.

text_fidelity_a:
VP Components VP-Vice Pedals (Pack of 2) There are some interesting patterns that you'll see if you read through the reviews. Some people recevied their pedals shrink wrapped, and they scratch the other pedal in transport. Some people get new pedals in a box, and life is wonderful because they got an awesome pedal set at an awesome price. And some people get pedals in a box that look brand new, but have blown bearings. I'm in that third group.

I bought this pair from cyclingdeal_usa, fulfilled by Amazon. I was happy to see the pedals arrive looking brand new in a box similar to the one my first Vices showed up in about five years ago. I'm a huge fan of these pedals, and the fact that I have a the titanium pins for my primary bike, and that they're now as ridiculously affordable as they are means it makes sense to put these on the other bikes in the house.

I bought these for my son's bike, and the look great, but there was a click with each stroke on the left pedal. I threw them on my bike, on the titanium pins, and there was still a click with each stroke. I changed out the bearings (I had a rebuild kit on hand) and boom, the pedals are exactly as they should be, and the click is gone.

Like some other people's reviews, my VP-Vice Pedal set showed up with blown bearings. The right pedal was fine, but the left pedal clicked out of the box, and that's the first time I've seen a pair of Vice pedals do that. I see they're currently at the best price through VP Components. I'm hopeful that means they're shipped in a new box, and that if there's any issues, I know from a past experience with them, that VP Components will make it right.

I'm rating this purchase 4*, because I love the pedals, I love VP components, and I'm very happy with the bang for the buck of getting all my bikes on Vice pedals, but I hate that I had to use my rebuild kit to get working bearings in left pedal. (Yeah, I know I could have returned them, but I wanted to get them on my son's new bike, and we were all excited to go riding.)
text_fidelity_b: VP Components VP-Vice Pedals (Pack of 2)

text_fidelity_a:
Sunny Health & Fitness SF-E902 Air Walk Trainer Elliptical Machine Glider w/LCD Monitor, 220 LB Max Weight and 30 Inch Stride My husband just bought me the Sunny Air Walk Trainer, and it arrived yesterday. The box was so damaged that we were concerned there might be damage to the unit, but everything was fine. My husband had it put together in 10 minutes, leaving off the pad at my request. It's very quiet, quiet enough to chat over in a low voice, and the action is smooth. The time/distance display works fine, although I'd have rather it showed distance rather than number of individual motions back and forth.

This gives a no-impact workout, which is great if you're prone to shin splits or have bad knees. Unlike a lot of other fitness equipment, the foot pedals stay level with the floor, sort of like roller skating, which I find a big plus. On the other hand, I'm only 5' 3", but the stride is on the short side for me; not too short, but it took a little time to adjust. There's no resistance, so while it did get my heart pumping, I wouldn't think this would be as useful for someone fit who does a lot of cardio. For someone like me, recovering and overweight, it's fine.

One thing worth considering is that whenever you walk, jog or run, your weight is off each foot as you lift it to take the next step. With the Sunny Air Walk Trainer - or any other similar unit including the Gazelle - your weight is constantly on both feet. If you're overweight or have weak knees, this may be a concern.

The Air Walk Trainer is fairly well made - much better than I expected. It's also nice and small. I didn't even bother to fold it up - just pushed it into a corner. And this has to be one of the best values in fitness equipment - under $100, strong, made of metal, smooth action. If you don't have room for a treadmill or recumbent exercise bike and are looking for a lighter workout, I'd definitely consider this.

BTW, I'll update this review after I've had the Air Walk Trainer for a while.

Edit: After using this for a few months, I sold my Air Walk Trainer because I found that even at 5' 3", the stride is too short for me to really get going. Years ago, I had a Gazelle, and with that, I was able to use my full stride of 22", but with the reduced stride length of the Air Walk Trainer, I always felt constrained. Still, if that doesn't bother you, it's a decent piece of equipment. For my use, I'd give this 3 stars, but for others who don't mind shortening their stride, it's a 4.
text_fidelity_b: Sunny Health & Fitness SF-E902 Air Walk Trainer Elliptical Machine Glider w/LCD Monitor, 220 LB Max Weight and 30 Inch Stride

Mountain House Chicken & Dumplings with Vegetables This is just astonishingly easy to make and it tastes way better than expected. Usually dehydrated foods are flavorless and lifeless, but this chicken and dumpling concoction actually smells like chicken when you open the package and you can recognize the peas & carrots immediately. (see the photo)

I added the cup and a half of boiling water to the pouch per the directions, sealed the pouch and let it cook for 12 minutes. Opening the pouch releases a chickeny aroma and everything is sort of mushy and definitely cooked and ready to eat. The texture is fine - the chicken chunks are edible and not rubbery at all. The carrots & peas are fine as well. The only issue was with some of the dumplings - these are made of biscuits instead of noodle based and some of them were actually a bit crunchy. I'm not sure if this was deliberate or if maybe I should have used a little more water than the directions suggest. There's not real broth with the cup and a half - it's more like a bowl of porridge. The flavor is good and I didn't need to add any salt to this at all. I would consider adding a couple of these to our Hurricane Emergency supply kit for sure.

Perfect Life Ideas 3 Pack Camping Lanterns LED Lamps Emergency Lights for Home Vehicle Travel Emergencies - Garage Office Desk Camp Rv Boat. Battery Operated Lighting Gear. Cordless. Brand Tm These are small - roughly the same size as a coke can - and that makes them the perfect size for some very specific uses. They weigh almost nothing, even with the four AA batteries inserted. The little handle on top is just tall enough to hang these lanterns from a drawer pull or in our house, a push down style door knob. With the light weight, the lantern hangs without affecting the use of the door handle so you can have light in an interior room or basement while hunting for a fuse box etc and know where the exit is. I also like that the exterior of the lantern is a bit of a rubberized texture - setting it on our marble bathroom counter in the dark wasn't as risky as it would've been with just slick plastic. These are small and weigh very little - a slippery surface or wet hands could be a problem without the textured case.

The light is very bright and clear white. No yellow hue to it at all and these LED bulbs turn on instantly. We tested the lights in a pitch black garage, closet and walking around in the back yard at 11pm. They are bright enough to use to get dressed or find your way around the garage with no problems at all. Use in the yard was fine, but a flashlight is better as a directional aimed beam for walking. My one star deduction is because I dropped one of the lanterns from hip high and it came apart when it landed (a fall of two feet onto a thick bath mat). The batteries flew out and the bottom cracked apart. However - the light DID work afterwards and we just super glued the crack back together. I'll keep these in the bathroom, garage and kitchen for power outages in the future. I received a sample set for testing and review.

BW Sports Fly Rod and Reel Case for (10 Ft.) 2-Piece Fly Rods - RC 1010 Ok but needs some design improvement. Just returned from a trout fishing vacation and used two of these on my trip. Both were for 10 foot rods. The case is actually pretty good considering the price. However, the tube should have some relief cut length wise (4" or so) into the top end to assist in removing the rod. The rod has to be removed straight out the back without any angle but the pouch itself interferes to some degree. A 4" or so notch cut out at the top end would facilitate easy removal. The little storage pouches on the sides might be a nice touch for some but to me they were an unnecessary nuisance. Also, a nice dense closed cell foam fly patch would be nice.

CAUTION: I broke an Orivs 10 foot rod right off the bat putting it in this case. I use this type of case so that I can pull the rod down into two pieces, keep the reel on with the leader and fly so that all I have to do is put it together the next pull over or stream. That is the point of having the reel pouch. When I placed the rod into the case, apparently the tip went into one compartment and the butt into another. When I pushed the r\od all the way in the line came tight against the compartments and snapped the very tip of the rod....My bad, but just a word of caution. I now make certain that both sections of rod go into ONE compartment.
text_fidelity_b: BW Sports Fly Rod and Reel Case for (10 Ft.) 2-Piece Fly Rods - RC 1010

ATIVAFIT Adjustable Dumbbell Set Free Weights Dumbbell Multiweight Options for Men Women Full Body Workout Fitness Home Gym I recently retired from a physical job and did not want to "let myself go', so I've decided to get some things around the house to help keep myself on some kind of decent shape.

This set of dumbbells is just the ticket for a variety of weights when you have a limited space. The set I have ranges in weight from 11 pounds to 66 pounds per dumbbell. That's more than enough to keep me occupied for quite some time, trust me. I had seen sets like this before and thought the concept to be somewhat odd, but now that I have a set I can definitely see the benefits. Years ago, I had a pair of dumbbell handles and lots of free weights that I could put on them for various configurations. Yeah, it gave you plenty of options, but you still had to have room to store not only the dumbbells themselves, but also the wieghts that were not in use at the time. This setup is much more convenient.

These each come with a form-fit rack to set them in while not in use as well as when you are changing weights. A simple push of the red button and then twist the dial at the end to whatever weight you desire, and the handle releases or grabs whichever plates needed to make that weight. Lift the dumbbell and the unneeded plates stay standing right in the stand. When you are done, the dumbbell slides right back into place. You never need more space for storage than the dumbbells themselves.

They were a bit unnerving to use at first because I had a subconscious tendency to not trust weights that "wiggle", but that soon went away. I have never had an instance where a plate fell. I think the key is just to double check that the plates are truly locked in place when adjusting them.

These things are built quite well and I have zero complaints about the craftsmanship. They look as good as they function. Obviously, with the materials that there are constructed with, they will probably outlast me.
text_fidelity_b: ATIVAFIT Adjustable Dumbbell Set Free Weights Dumbbell Multiweight Options for Men Women Full Body Workout Fitness Home Gym

text_fidelity_a:
Etekcity Water Filter Straw Camping Water Purification Portable Water Filter Survival Kit for Camping, Hiking, Hurricanes I've had this on my bug-out list for a while now. At last I got it. I had questions I had doubts, because I was at first thinking of this as a filtration system. Yes it filtrates water.... no it is not a general filtration system. It is a "Personal" filter. A sip straw with advantages. Emphasis on the 'sip'. If you got as far as the comments section, you've seen what they say about it. This is for hiking, rather than camping use. Something to get water from point A to your mouth. However.... I did want to find out if I could use the bag to filter water into a cup for heating and it DOES work! You fill the bag with water... as clear as you can find, screw it into the straw, and gently but firmly squeeze. Filtered water will slowly dribble out of the sipping end. Not fast, but if you need a cup of coffee or some soup, it would be worth it. We are not talking kitchen magic here folks, we are talking survival.
To make this last as long as possible, use the clearest water you can find, use the little blue add-on filter, and backwash every time you use it. Just remember, water from a street gutter is not a good source, because of all the chemical contaminates that might be in it. This is for dirt, microbes, and insect contamination, not oil, anti-freeze and cleaners!
Picture 1 shows the bag screwed into the base, 2 shows the long folded tube attached to the base. you can also take off the short tube from the blue filter and attach it to the end of the long tube. Picture 3 shows the blue filter and the disk replacement filters for it (you get 6 total), and 4 shows the back-flow set-up. The plunger tube snugs 'into' not 'over' the mouth piece and the small blue filter's tube as well.

This was one of the Eteckcity products that I could get free or at reduced price in exchange for a review. I won't 'guess' if it works I won't say something I don't believe. This my honest opinion of a product I acquired to use personally.
text_fidelity_b: Etekcity Water Filter Straw Camping Water Purification Portable Water Filter Survival Kit for Camping, Hiking, Hurricanes

text_fidelity_a:
ALPS Mountaineering Ready Lite Cot (WARNING- In depth review- if you want a shorter summary, see section marked THE BOTTOM LINE)

We have a lot of occasions in our family where one or more of us need to have a small portable cot or bed to take with us in camping or work camp situations. We have tried the inflatable mattresses, but they deflate and are not always able to be re-inflated easily in certain locations. This bed was attractive because it packs small, is portable, keeps you off the ground, and is long enough to accommodate most of us height-wise.

WHAT IS THIS COT LIKE?
This cot comes in a small package which zips shut. It is made from the same dark gray nylon that the cot is made of and has a good strong zipper. Inside is a nylon label sewn into the bag which has instructions with excellent illustrations on how to put the bed together. There is a space to put the shock corded poles in which separates it from the cot fabric but a nylon divider in the bag. That enables the cot to be transported easily so that it does not eventually wear spots in the cot itself by poles rubbing on it.

HOW DOES THIS COT GO TOGETHER?
This is where we took off one star for this. The cot is great. The problem is that it took two of us 30 minutes the first time to get the long straight poles in the sides because it was just so tight of a fit. There was no way that any of us could do this alone and we have pretty good hand and arm strength.

Once we finally got the straight poles in, we did not find any problem snapping the legs onto the frame. As long as you put some weight on them, they bend just enough to snap onto the frame.

HOW DOES THIS COT FEEL/PERFORM?
This cot is quite comfortable for what it is. I personally prefer a mat on top, but our daughter is preferring to sleep on it as it it. My husband likes it either way and the rest of the kids are too large for it. If you sleep with a pillow it is nice, but even without a pillow it is still pretty nice. It is also nice for stomach sleeping as well as back. Side sleeping I did feel pressure points after a bit, but I was not able to test it with a mat- only pillows which I would not be carrying with me on trips.

COMMENTS
Over time I am expecting this cot to go together a little easier as it is used, hopefully the fabric will give and the long poles won't be so hard to put in the pockets. So far, it is still a struggle as we have used it a few times.

LENGTH
We found that this fit those of us up to 6 ft tall easily and comfortably, but two people who wanted to try it were too large for it- being about 6 ft 4 inches and about 385-400 pounds, and another in a similar weight/height range. This is more for people who are 6 ft and below and not very overweight.

WIDTH
This cot seems to be plenty wide enough to sleep on comfortably considering it was made for mountaineering.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Great cot for packing, and taking on camp and work camp tours, this cot is great for what we wanted to use it for. It supports the back nicely and is more comfortable than laying on the ground. Some might prefer a mat on top, but some of us preferred it as it is. It is very difficult for one person to put it together so don't plan on being in a hurry with it when you first get it. Hopefully it will continue to get easier over time.

MY RATING
I gave this four stars because of the difficulty in one person putting it together and how long it takes us for the side poles. However, it is more like 4 and a HALF stars. This cot is perfect for a small bed easy to keep you off the ground, yet be easy enough to sleep on.

Heck, even the cat likes it. He thinks it is for him whenever we put it up..
text_fidelity_b: ALPS Mountaineering Ready Lite Cot

text_fidelity_a:
Bixle 1/2-inch Extra Thick (15mm) 72-inch Long High Density Exercise Yoga Mat with Comfort Foam and Carrying Straps (Red) The first 2 weeks of use I loved this mat... but then I started to need a second mat to put on top of it. Many of the excercises I'm doing require that I stand on my knees and this mat provided great support... but after only a few days the imprint of my knees would stay on there longer and longer to the point where 24 hours later my knee prints are still there. Of coarse I move my knees around to different spots, but now my mat is full of knee prints. The mat gets thinner at these points and now my knee starts to hurt while I'm on the mat. I have to put an EXTRA mat on top of this one just so that it doesn't hurt now. I'm going to have to look for something sturdier that keeps it's thickness. In the meantime I've actually cut off the last 14" of the mat and use it to add extra cushioning for my knees while I'm using the mat. I'm short so I don't need the full length anyway.

I do think that this mat is great for yoga too and have had no problems doing so. However it's not good for a serious yoga practice because it's too thick and stretchy. For a casual practice it does fine.

You will then have a personalized fit and this is thick enough to keep you from grinding your teeth but not so thick that you can't close your mouth. And it is inexpensive - which is the best thing, I keep a few of these types around just in case I need one and my old one is ready to trash. This way, I never have to worry about going to sleep at night without a guard in my mouth. Having had to pay for crowns after breaking 3 teeth while on vacation one year, I learned to always wear a guard when I sleep.
text_fidelity_b: Franklin Sports Adult Mouth Guard (Assorted Colors)

Hand Warmers Rechargeable, 10000mAh Portable Electric Hand Warmer Power Bank, 3 Levels Adjustable LED Temperature Display, Best Gift for Winter It took me two days to figure this hand warmer out because the instructions did not tell me how to turn it off after I got it all heated up! This about had me worried until my husband figured out how to turn it off by reading how the heat was turned on in the first place. I'm so proud of him for figuring it out! Gotta love a man who can figure out this advanced technology! Ha!

So this hand warmer is made with silky soft material that feels comfortable in your hands. It is not too heavy. If you are however trying this out and your hands are already warm it is going to feel very hot. When my hands were super cold today I tried it out again and it was perfectly comfortable on all three heat settings. This will give you three levels of heat - Low/Medium/High!

How to Operate - This should all be in the instruction manual! I finally figured it out.

Left Button - Press once to see power charge display up to 100% power.

Left Button - Press twice to turn off display - screen will go dark.

Right Button - Making sure left button has turned off display - long press the right button for
five seconds to turn heat on. It will start flashing and show heat level. This is
warm enough most of the time for hands not in gloves.

Left Button - Now press the left button to increase heat even more. If this
is fine leave it here on the second level. If you need it warmer go to next step.

Right Button - Now press right button and heat goes up to the third level.

Done with heating your hands? Now turn it off by long pressing the right button for
five seconds. Screen will stop flashing and go off - dark screen.

That is how to operate this and I'm keeping the instructions around for next year when I've probably forgotten it all again!

So this would make a wonderful gift to someone you love. Just give them these instruction because otherwise they won't be able to figure out how to turn the unit off!

I also charged the unit after it reached 75% power and it only took a few hours. This comes nearly fully charged so it can be used right out of the box.

Happy Hand Warming!

~The Rebecca Review
text_fidelity_b: Hand Warmers Rechargeable, 10000mAh Portable Electric Hand Warmer Power Bank, 3 Levels Adjustable LED Temperature Display, Best Gift for Winter

Rechargeable Camping Lantern, Collapsible 2200mah Battery Powered LED Lights for Tents, 3 in 1 IP66 Waterproof Emergency Flashlight for Camping, Hiking, Hunting, Outages, Outdoor, Garden I have been trying to get various bug zappers to bring with my family when we go to areas that are not close to a plug. This one is interesting. Let's take a look.

HOW THIS COMES
This comes in a small box with instructions.

CLOSED
Closed this is used for a light. It has brighter white light, dimmed light and a warning red light.

OPEN
Open this has the ability to zap bugs.

HOW WELL DOES THIS PERFORM?
This performs well as a light, but as a bug zapper, it really is not the season for heavy bugs like we will be having later in the season. I have not been able to catch the few tiny moths in the house, nor the few tiny fruit flies. That is no surprise, however, because this zapper is not very big and these guys have been all over the house.

The light part is nice for using when necessary to see at night. During power outages it also will be handy.

HOW THIS RUNS
This runs not only on USB charging,, but also works with AAA batteries(3) which don't come with it.

CHARGE TIME
This took a couple of hours to charge up fully and it lasts a few hours depending on how it is used. I usually charge after that, so I have not let it run completely down yet.

CAN IT HANG FROM CENTER OF TENT?
This does make a good light for hanging from the center of the tent when you want to see with an overhead light. It also would do well in that position as a bug zapper. It has a handle so you can twist tie it to the loops.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For using at a camp site or on a deck in summer, this is a nice little light to have at the table at night, or use for walking at night around a camp site. As for bug zapper, in the tent, I would have to have some eye masks to sleep with. The light would be too bright for me to sleep with.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS. If this turns out to be a bug zapping wonder, I will stop by and update my rating on this zapper/light. As it is now, it works, seems to do what it is supposed to do, but situations are not dire enough to see how good it really is.
text_fidelity_b: Rechargeable Camping Lantern, Collapsible 2200mah Battery Powered LED Lights for Tents, 3 in 1 IP66 Waterproof Emergency Flashlight for Camping, Hiking, Hunting, Outages, Outdoor, Garden

Tour Edge Bazooka 360 Men's Varsity Box Full Set, Right Hand, Black/Blue At first, I was very excited I’m able to get a well-known golf brand for my son’s first complete set. I’ve had Tour Edge drivers and fairway woods before (Exotics line), love the quality. But in this set, it left a lot to be desired. The quality is reminiscent of knock off brands: on some clubs (mainly the woods and hybrid) paint on the heads were misaligned, surfaces looked wavy, some zippers on the bag wouldn’t close because the tracks were off, and some other minor things not worth mentioning. Aside from many quality issues, the one that stood out the most are the dents on some club faces. This is a brand new set, why does it have dents? The bubble wrap and packaging were acceptable and it looked well packaged, there’s no reason for having dents. Quality issue? I’ve had clubs that were at least 10 years old and have been beat up; aside from superficial scratches, those clubs still were dent-free and serviceable. The set is slightly more expensive than some no-name beginner sets but I’m thinking the quality could be comparable. I get it, it’s a teen set, but I expected better quality control from the Tour Edge name. As I’m writing this, I’m actually pondering if this could be a knock off set, I hope not.
The good thing is that it is a complete set, the irons were of better quality it seems, and although the bag seems flimsy, it’s very light and will help with walking the course.

text_fidelity_a:
Mars Gear Vulcan FLX Tactical Pants (Stretchable Ripstop) [[VIDEOID:b5a53a0c1b472799ef4d5a2d386537bd]] I like certain things about these and can't stand certain other ones. I cannot stand the location of the pockets. They are way too high and closer to the center. They could have cut it at more of a slant but it still is too high. You got to put your hands almost straight down into them. While this is good for stopping some pick pockets they are still open, There should be a zipper secured side pocket inside the main pocket. These don't even have side pockets at all.

Now that;s out of the way it has a lot of pockets almost too many or they are not quite big enough to hold what you need them too.. The zipper in the front doesn't stay up unless zipped all the way and locked, so you;ll end up with your fly down if your not careful and don't make sure to get the zipper all the way up, This is waste time,. in my opinion, at least. The belt loops are too small to even accommodate an 2 inch utility belt.

These are very comfortable and just about the proper warmth and cooling so they are good year round unless you live in Alaska , Siberia or any place that get below -10 degrees Fahrenheit on a regular basis. I never really got uncomfortably hot or cold in these. Some of the stitching is top notch and then there are others that are terrible. The inside of the pocket are horribly stitched and I have never seen poor stitching on any good pair of BDU's or any other military or law enforcement pant types called "tactical".

I really like the ties around the legs that allow you to tie the legs tight either around your leg inside your boots or over the outside of your boot. This is good for limiting bugs crawling up your pant legs and various other things. Now they should've used some elastic ropes with a little fast tightener in place of the cheap ribbon. There is also no loop on the waste back close to your pocket to clip anything to.

So I have decided that these are just not very good the more and more I try them out. They just feel like everything is slightly out of place. One more thing the belt loops will not accommodate any decent utility belts or even a thick well made gun belt. Not to mention I wouldn't trust the stitch-work either over any amount of time and duty. I usually wear 5.11 or Backhawk for civilian purposes and they never caused distractions. One of the two no longer is making gear and the other is slacking so I was looking for a new supplier. This was definitely not it. I think these are trying to be fashionable instead of tactical and you just cannot mix the two. Same goes for combat boots! If you are trying to look cool and have no real reason to need to wear BDU pants then go ahead and enjoy. If you require something that actually provides performance and functionality then these are not for you. I couldn't wear these to the range let alone any real situation.
text_fidelity_b: Mars Gear Vulcan FLX Tactical Pants (Stretchable Ripstop)

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin vívofit 4 activity tracker with 1+ year battery life and color display. Large, Black. 010-01847-03 I love the app. It’s super user-friendly, and offers clear menus with your collected info, with options to connect with social media, plot running trails, and find popular places to walk/jog. If I were reviewing this solely on the app, this product would easily earn five stars,

BUT....

The data is 100% off. This is probably the most inaccurate fitness tracker I’ve used so far, both for step counts and sleep tracking. I used it for a little over a week to see if it could “learn”, or if different activities tracked more accurately, and it was pretty inconsistent.

Steps: I set a goal of 7,000 steps, which with my other trackers was a High goal. I could teach/take 3 hours of cardio-heavy dance and have regular activities other than that like cleaning up the house, doing office stuff, checking mail, etc, and I would *sometimes* get to 7,000. That’s Three Hours of cardio. Meanwhile, the last week has been full of house renovating, but that mostly consisted of staying in one place and repairing things, organizing things, and making runs to the hardware store. It did NOT consist of many steps or a bunch of walking. Even so, it said I made it to something around 9,000 steps. There is No Way I took that many steps. If I had to guess, I *maybe* made it to 5k. All week has been the same, with Very exaggerated counts.

Sleep: fail. More than half the nights, it showed no data at all and advised me to wear the band. I have literally not removed this thing even once in over a week, not even for showering. Other nights, it said I slept 8.5 hours, when I know I slept under four. I remembered the time I turned everything off and closed my eyes it was around 4am. I woke up around 8am. The phone said I was asleep by 11:30ish. Another night, it said I slept 10 hours, from 8pm-6-am. I can’t think of a time in the last decade that I’ve gone to bed at 8. I am practically a vampire. And that was on a day I finally got to sleep in, so I woke up at around 11. When I tried editing the data in hopes of teaching it, the system was buggy. I saved and exited the screen, and it went right back to the incorrect stuff. This would happen a few times, and in the end, I was only able to correct one of the nights successfully. I don’t have the energy to keep trying. Maybe it will get better, maybe not, but I’m not doing extra data entry work for this.

So all in all, I can’t recommend this product. The data is consistently wrong, which makes it practically impossible to assess what you’re doing or not doing.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin vívofit 4 activity tracker with 1+ year battery life and color display. Large, Black. 010-01847-03

The Fridge Drink Cooler - Lifoam If you like cold drinks, this is the ultimate coozie to get! They not only keep your drinks cold for hours, but they can actually make your drinks colder than they were from the refrigerator!

That is because each coozie has two main layers that work together to chill the drinks: an inner gel layer and a thick outer styrofoam layer.

When you put the coozie in the freezer, the gel layer freezes. This layer can actually drop the temperature of whatever drink you put int the coozie. It's like wrapping your drink in a blanket of ice! Then the styrofoam layer makes sure all that great coldness stays there. Drinks normally stay cold for several hours!

Another nice feature when using these coozies is that there is no problem with leaving wet rings on the furniture because the coozies prevent the normal condensation problem you have with cold drinks in a warm environment. I think this is because of the thick insulation layer. The cold inside is insulated from the warm outside which prevents condensation.

I know these coozies last for years. I originally found these coozies on MisterCold.com in 2006 and used them constantly ever since. I have taken them with me everywhere I go. They have held up very well for so much use. After 7 years of use, they finally began to show signs of wear (slight fraying at the bottom) so I decided it was time to get new ones. I was thrilled to find them here on Amazon! The new ones I got are just as good, if not better, than the original ones I bought years ago.

If you want to enjoy drinks that are cold, cold, cold and stay that way for hours, this is the perfect item for you. Just be sure to get a bunch because once your family and friends try them, they'll use them all the time. So you need plenty on hand to be sure there's always a cold one waiting for you! text_fidelity_a: SABRE Stun Gun 3-In-1 Safety Tool, 1.154 Microcoulombs (µC) Charge, 115 dB Personal Alarm, Audible Up To 1,000-Feet (305-Meters), 70 Lumen Flashlight, Includes Wrist Strap While tempted I haven't zapped myself with this and none of my friends are willing to let me test this on them. It does make a reasonably loud zappy sound when you trigger it but I have no idea how effective it is. What I can report having tested are the flashlight and siren. Flashlight at full charge is good enough to help you find a lock in the dark or something you might have dropped but it's not very bright or focused. Just a dim widely spread beam. I don't think the siren would do much to frighten a criminal away, it's barely loud enough to be annoying. A mugger is likely to just hit you and take it away. It might work as a signal device if you fell and needed help. Another problem with this is all three switches; light, siren and stun gun are pink, the marking icon on the buttons are small and hard to distinguish. In an emergency figuring out which button is which could mean a lot. The siren and stun functionality also have an on/off switch on the base that needs to be activated before either feature can be used (the flashlight function is always available). The big problem with the switch is it stands quite proud of the base and can easily be bumped or nudge on, then you have a live stun gun in your pocket and a button that also easily pressed as you fumble this out of your pocket. I can just imagine resting your hand on your leg and shocking yourself completely by accident. If the 'safety' switch were flush or covered in some way to make it hard to accidentally activate I might have rated it higher. As it stands it's just as dangerous to the owner as it is to a would be attacker, maybe more so.
text_fidelity_b: SABRE Stun Gun 3-In-1 Safety Tool, 1.154 Microcoulombs (µC) Charge, 115 dB Personal Alarm, Audible Up To 1,000-Feet (305-Meters), 70 Lumen Flashlight, Includes Wrist Strap
